FACT_HOOK: These high-speed particles may subtly influence life itself.
FACT_EXPLANATION: Cosmic rays can penetrate living tissue, causing mutations in DNA. While most mutations are harmless or lethal, rare beneficial ones drive evolution. Elevated cosmic ray flux during supernova events or weakened solar magnetic shields could increase mutation rates on Earth. Some researchers speculate that periodic bursts of cosmic rays contributed to evolutionary leaps or extinctions over millions of years. Early microbial life endured a more intense cosmic bombardment due to a thinner atmosphere and weaker magnetic field, shaping adaptation pathways. Today, high-altitude pilots, astronauts, and even airline passengers receive slightly elevated doses, though mostly negligible. Cosmic rays act as invisible agents of change, linking astrophysical events to biology. Understanding this influence merges astrophysics, genetics, and evolutionary biology. It’s a reminder that the universe doesn’t just surround us; it subtly nudges life along its evolutionary path.
IMPACT_PARAGRAPH_1: Cosmic rays may have contributed to genetic mutations and evolutionary processes on Earth.
IMPACT_PARAGRAPH_2: They highlight a deep, unexpected connection between cosmic phenomena and biology.
DID_YOU_KNOW: Cosmic rays can cause DNA mutations, potentially influencing evolution and adaptation.
